findings.title: Validator has a database write side effect and runs on every validation
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at` and saves the record. It is called from inside a validator, which runs on every `valid?` call. In `UsersController#create`, `user.valid?` is called and then `user.save` validates again, so a single signup attempt increments the counter twice. Validation also writes to the DB even when the user is never saved, and the write sits inside the save transaction, so it is rolled back if the save fails. The statistics are therefore unreliable, and validation is no longer free of side effects.

findings.title: Email lookup is case-sensitive and not normalized
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` does an exact-case match, but emails are case-insensitive in practice and elsewhere in the codebase are downcased via `Email.downcase`. A blocked address like `bad@spam.com` can be bypassed by signing up as `Bad@Spam.com`. Neither the stored value nor the lookup value is normalized. A nil email passed to the validator is also not handled.

findings.title: Non-atomic read-modify-write on match_count
findings.body: `record.match_count += 1` followed by `save` is a lost-update race under concurrent signups. Use `update_all`, or an atomic `match_count = match_count + 1`, instead. The save also ignores its return value.

findings.title: Validator crashes on nil/blank values and the record is not checked for missing attributes
findings.body: `validate_each` runs the whitelist/blacklist regexp and `BlockedEmail.should_block?` on `value` without a nil guard. `value =~ regexp` with a nil value returns nil, so the whitelist branch wrongly adds a "not allowed" error on top of the presence error. Skipping blank values (`allow_blank`) would avoid this.

findings.title: rejectedEmails array is shared across all controller instances
findings.body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is defined on the prototype in `extend`, so the same array object is shared by every instance, and entries are never cleared. Rejected emails persist for the lifetime of the page and across instances. Initialize it in `init`. The `.property('accountEmail', 'rejectedEmails.@each')` dependency key is also non-standard for this Ember version.

findings.title: Any email error is treated as a rejected email, with a generic message
findings.body: `result.errors.email` is truthy for any email error, including "has already been taken" or a malformed address. The email is then marked locally as invalid with the generic `user.email.invalid` text. The user sees no explanation of why it was blocked. The server's actual reason is not surfaced in the field validation.

findings.title: No tests for whitelist/blacklist behavior or the end-to-end user validation path
findings.body: The whitelist/blacklist logic was moved from User into the validator, but the new spec only covers the blocked-email stub. The existing domain restriction behavior and the skipping of the blocked check when a domain error is already present are not tested. The controller's new `errors`/`values` response fields and the validation counting behavior are also untested.
